title: Number of Spaces Cleaning Robot Cleaned
summary: Given a 2D binary matrix representing a room, where 0s are empty spaces and 1s are spaces with objects, a robot starting at the top left corner and facing right cleans spaces by moving straight until hitting an object or the edge, then turning 90 degrees clockwise.
statement: Given a 2D binary matrix representing a room, where 0s are empty spaces and 1s are spaces with objects, a robot starting at the top left corner and facing right cleans spaces by moving straight until hitting an object or the edge, then turning 90 degrees clockwise. Continue this process indefinitely. Return the total number of cleaned spaces.
constraints: room is a nonempty binary matrix and room[0][0] is empty.
The robot starts at top-left facing right, moves forward when possible, otherwise turns clockwise in place.
Return the number of distinct empty cells cleaned before its behavior repeats forever.
hints: Movement is deterministic, so repeating the same cell and direction means the entire future will repeat.
Simulate while tracking full states and a separate set of cleaned cells.
On blockage rotate direction=(direction+1)%4; otherwise move; stop at repeated (row,column,direction).
There are only four states per cell, guaranteeing termination, and deterministic state repetition proves no new cell can appear afterward.
editorial: There are only four states per cell, guaranteeing termination, and deterministic state repetition proves no new cell can appear afterward.

tests.explanation: The deterministic route reaches seven distinct empty cells before repeating a state.
The robot cleans only its starting cell.
